clue.text: Mature women's gathering outside

indicators.note: the gathering sits outside, wrapping round the letter for women

parts.note: a gathering of people is a group
W is the standard abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Grown women form a circle in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: To mature is to become adult, the same as the phrasal verb meaning reach adulthood.

clue.text: His services are provided on the house

definitions.text: His services are provided on the house

parts.words: His services are provided on the house
parts.note: on the house usually means free of charge, but here it means literally on top of the building

explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who repairs roofs does his work up on the house itself.

clue.text: Change male into amusing, fanciful sort

indicators.note: the first pieces go into the word for amusing

parts.note: witty means amusing, clever with words
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: Turn a man into a funny, imaginative character.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Mitty is the daydreaming hero of a James Thurber story, whose name now means a fantasist.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of Thurber's daydreamer is used for anyone who lives in elaborate fantasies.

clue.text: Member of ambulance crew trained to give camper aid

indicators.note: trained, as in drilled into shape, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ambulance worker learns first aid at a campsite.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramedic is a medically trained worker who staffs an ambulance.

clue.text: Sets of flyers publicise sea-trip through sound

parts.note: to air an idea is to publicise it

indicators.note: the word sound tells us the next piece is spelt as it is heard, not as written

parts.note: a sea-trip on a liner is a cruise

explanation.surface: Pilots announce a holiday voyage over the tannoy.
explanation.walkthrough: CRUISE said out loud matches CREWS; 'through' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Teams of people who staff an aircraft are its crews, so groups of flying staff are aircrews.

clue.text: David's boy, a born dancer, but losing footing

indicators.note: the foot, or last letter, of the word is dropped

parts.note: Salome danced before Herod in the Bible story

explanation.surface: King David's son was a natural dancer but kept stumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the 'footing' is the bottom letter, so SALOME loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Absalom was a son of King David in the Old Testament who rebelled against him.

clue.text: European state headed by king

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
Oman is a state in Arabia

explanation.surface: A European country with a monarch at its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headed by' places the king's letter on top of the state in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman, an inhabitant of Rome, is a European.

clue.text: Control athletic event

definitions.meaning: to manage or be in charge of, as in a business

explanation.definitionFit: To run a company is to control it; a run is also a race in athletics.

clue.text: Desire, but in lascivious way

parts.note: to want is to desire
only can mean but, as in 'I'd come, only I am busy'

explanation.surface: Wishes that are nonetheless lustful.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantonly means lewdly or without restraint, as a lascivious person behaves.

clue.text: Markers from examination bodies receive fifty pounds

indicators.note: the boards take in the two letters, holding them inside

parts.note: exam boards set and mark school examinations
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
L (libra) is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Examiners get a fee of fifty pounds for marking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Markers' suggests examiners, but it means posts that mark out a road or quay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bollards are short posts used to mark out traffic lanes or tie up boats, so they serve as markers.

clue.text: Mother and grandmother meeting later in Spain

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
nana is a familiar word for grandmother

explanation.surface: Mum and Gran arrange to get together some time on a Spanish holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for tomorrow is used loosely to mean some indefinite later time.

clue.text: Avoid pawn loss? Think again

definitions.meaning: to get back a pawned item by paying off the loan, so you do not lose it
read as ..., to deem a second time

explanation.definitionFit: Redeeming a pledge recovers it from the pawnbroker; split up, the word means to judge anew.

clue.text: Cricketer has strong desire to play at first

parts.note: someone who longs for something has a strong desire for it

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word play is used

explanation.surface: A cricketer is itching to get on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: LONG STOP is a fielding position in cricket, behind the wicketkeeper near the boundary, and so also the fielder there.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder placed in that deep position behind the keeper is a member of the cricket side.

clue.text: It provides a measure of the progress one makes in one's driving

definitions.text: It provides a measure of the progress one makes in one's driving

parts.words: It provides a measure of the progress one makes in one's driving
parts.note: reads like an assessment of a learner's skill, but means a dial showing how fast a car travels

explanation.definitionFit: The dashboard instrument shows the rate at which the car is moving.

clue.text: Nice young lady?

parts.note: Nice is the French Riviera city, so a young woman there is addressed in French

explanation.definitionFit: The French title for an unmarried young woman is what you would call a girl in Nice.

clue.text: Ban criminal, tried in court

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A felon is barred after trial in court.
explanation.definitionFit: An interdict is a formal prohibition, especially a legal or church one.

clue.text: Drink heavily, left out of musical

parts.note: to carouse is to drink and make merry

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker walked out of a West End show.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: take L out of the musical and you are left with the drinking verb, so the pieces join as CAROUSE plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousel is the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical.

clue.text: Was involved in early stage, before CID head came in

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second in the answer

parts.note: Part I is the first, early stage of a work

indicators.note: the word for head enters the letters CID, sitting inside them

parts.note: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, taken as written
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: A detective was present at the start of a case before the head of CID arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'CID head' reads as the chief of detectives, but CID and head are separate pieces: PATE goes inside CID to make CIPATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To participate is to take part, so the past tense means took part or was involved.

clue.text: Set to work, havin' ups and downs in the main

definitions.meaning: to join in and get busy

definitions.text: havin' ups and downs in the main
definitions.meaning: a ship pitching in the sea rises and falls; the dropped g is shown by the apostrophe

explanation.definitionFit: To pitch in is to start work energetically; a ship that is pitching in the main rocks fore and aft.

clue.text: Death of young lady, finally lost in river

indicators.note: the shortened lady goes in the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word, and lost says that letter is dropped

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl drowned in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Demise is a formal word for death.

clue.text: Scriptures worthily translated

indicators.note: translated suggests the letters are rendered into another form, a reordering

explanation.surface: Sacred texts rendered faithfully into English.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy writ is a traditional name for the Bible and other sacred writings.

clue.text: Manageress has taken up role at Stratford

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read upwards, so backwards
the word manageress has the letters within it

explanation.surface: A theatre manageress has been given a part in a Stratford production.
explanation.walkthrough: Stratford-upon-Avon is Shakespeare's birthplace; Regan is one of King Lear's daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: Regan is a character in Shakespeare's King Lear, staged at Stratford.

clue.text: Stranger given drinking glass

definitions.meaning: more odd or peculiar, comparative of rum meaning odd
a large old-fashioned goblet for drinks

explanation.definitionFit: Rum is British slang for odd, giving a comparative; the same spelling names a large stemmed drinking cup.

clue.text: Making request in royal manner

parts.note: in the manner of, like, meaning as
a king is a royal person

explanation.surface: Issuing a demand in a regal fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in royal manner' splits as AS (in the manner of) plus KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking is the act of putting a request to someone.

clue.text: Fish I had eaten for starters

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: for starters means only the opening letter of the word eaten is used

explanation.surface: A diner says a fish dish was the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I had' contracts to I'D, and 'for starters' takes only the E of 'eaten'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: By centre of Newhaven, I sell out of English fish

indicators.note: the middle two letters of the town name Newhaven are taken
the abbreviation for English is taken out of the word for sell

parts.note: to retail goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: Someone in a port town sells English fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Newhaven is a port on the English south coast; its centre is HA. E taken out of RETAIL gives RTAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The hairtail is a long, thin sea fish with a tapering whip-like tail.

clue.text: Angler troubled about boy's name

indicators.note: troubled signals the letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A fisherman fretting over what to call his son.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon is a traditional English given name for a boy.

clue.text: Country knight eluded old jailer

indicators.note: the knight escapes from the jailer, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a turnkey was an old word for a prison warder
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight escaped his warder somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is a nation straddling south-east Europe and western Asia.
